options.text: A permanent quota set by race and never reviewed again

options.misconception: prefers an unrecorded plan to a reviewable one
options.text: An informal preference stated privately and never written

options.misconception: removes personnel merit from hiring entirely
options.text: A rule handing all hiring decisions to the party chairman

questions.explanation: Programs that answer a specific past exclusion survive challenge when they state the goal, publish the criteria, and expire on schedule, which is why the durable ones were time-limited rather than open-ended. The tempting answer removes the written record that makes a plan reviewable at all.
questions.hint: What makes a program's own limits easy to check?

questions.subject: US_HISTORY
questions.learningObjective: analyze how a tax response intensified the loss of a city's tax base
questions.stem: In the 1970s a large city raised taxes to pay for schools, then watched wealthier families leave and its revenue fall again. Why did the response deepen the problem?

options.text: The taxes drove out the income the city depended on

options.misconception: reverses the direction of state-to-city financial aid
options.text: Higher taxes obliged the state to send the city more aid

options.misconception: claims crowding raised citywide property values
options.text: Crowded schools pushed property values up citywide

options.misconception: confuses population flight with staffing choices
options.text: The departure left the city more police and fewer residents

questions.explanation: Municipal finance leans on the taxable income of those who stay, so a tax aimed at departure accelerates departure and shrinks the base again, a self-reinforcing cycle rather than a one-time loss. The tempting answer reverses the direction of aid, when state law actually restricted such grants.
questions.hint: Who supplies the money a city collects?

questions.subject: US_HISTORY
questions.topic: Industrial retention after a plant closing
questions.learningObjective: design a plan that addresses the mechanism of a payroll loss
questions.stem: A mill town's largest employer announces it will close, and payroll taxes already fund half the city budget. Which plan attacks the actual mechanism of that loss?

options.text: Attract employers who need the same pool of skilled workers

options.misconception: answers a payroll loss with commemoration
options.text: Build a museum celebrating the mill and its machinery

options.misconception: cuts wages instead of finding the next employer
options.text: Cut the local wage so other firms will want to hire here

options.misconception: taxes commerce instead of rebuilding the base
options.text: Add a fee on every delivery truck entering the town

questions.explanation: The town's exposure runs through payrolls and the worker pool, so an incoming firm that needs the same skills works the same channel the closing mill did, whereas nostalgia or a wage cut changes nothing about who is willing to hire. The tempting answer undercuts demand for the very workers the plan needs to keep.
questions.hint: Through what channel does that closing reach the city budget?
